title: Ask-batch anecdote synthesis — May 2026
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working synthesis of recent customer anecdotes collected from support threads, onboarding calls, and a quick CS survey (n=42). Goal: convert raw anecdotes into clustered asks and sketch low-effort probes we can run in the next 2–4 weeks. Not a final prioritization; intended to seed engineering spikes and product experiments.

Executive one-liner:
Most customers describe three recurring pain patterns: (1) intermittent latency spikes during short bursts, (2) confusing behavior when model fallbacks happen, and (3) gaps in cache-hit visibility (they suspect KV/cache is helping but can’t measure). Fixes focused on observability + targeted fallbacks are highest ROI in the short term.

Method / sources:
- Support tickets (last 30 days) flagged with tags: latency, fallback, cache
- Onboarding call notes: 8 calls with mid-market and enterprise (sales recordings)
- CS survey prompt: “Biggest runtime friction last month?” (42 responses)
- Field engineers: 3 annotated incident timelines

Anecdote buckets (raw → synthesis):
1) Burst spike anecdotes (freq: high; pain: medium-high)
   - Raw: "Works fine for single requests; when traffic spikes for 10s of seconds latency jumps to 2x and timeouts." — infra engineer at ScaleApps
   - Synthesis: customers see short-lived tail latency that correlates with concurrent small bursts. Likely a scheduling/batching or autoscale cold path.
   - Quick probe: instrument request start-to-kernel timeline in prod sample, add a micro-trace field we can surface in Console.

2) Silent fallback confusion (freq: medium; pain: high)
   - Raw: "We started seeing answers change overnight; turns out traffic routed to smaller-quantized variant and we didn’t notice." — product manager at FinSolve
   - Synthesis: automatic fallback to cheaper model variants occurs without clear signals in Console or telemetry. Customers treat that as a regression / reliability issue.
   - Quick probe: add explicit model-variant header to response and a Console banner when fallbacks occur for >1% of requests in a 15m window.

3) KV-cache visibility and trust gap (freq: medium; pain: medium)
   - Raw: "We think cache saved tokens but can’t prove it; billing still looks weird." — growth lead at RetailGen
   - Synthesis: customers appreciate caching but lack easy, per-route cache-hit metrics and sample traces. That reduces willingness to apply aggressive cache policies.
   - Quick probe: expose per-route cache hit-rate, top 10 cached prefixes, and estimated token-savings in Console.

Representative quotes (verbatim):
- "We had to throttle the app because sometimes we hit a wall for 30s — it’s a black box."
- "Fallbacks are stealthy — our QA flagged model drift but ops said ’we scaled down’ and nobody knew why."
- "If I could see cache hits per request I’d be comfortable enabling prefix caching more widely."

Impact mapping (rough):
- Observability additions (console banners, headers, per-route metrics): low effort, high clarity for customers, immediate reduction in support noise.
- Fallback transparency (headers + rollout UI flags): medium effort, high trust impact for enterprises.
- Root cause for burst spikes (requires infra investigation): higher effort, but critical for SLO-sensitive customers — needs SRE/serving-runtime pairing.

Suggested low-effort deliverables (2–4 week horizons):
1) Response header: X-Redwood-Variant and X-Redwood-Fallback-Reason — propagate on all requests. (Owner: serving-runtime)
2) Console: small banner and a 15m-fold anomaly indicator when fallback rate > 1% (Owner: console-and-rollouts)
3) Console: add per-route KV-cache hit rate + estimated token savings (Owner: console-and-rollouts + observability)
4) Support playbook update: new quick triage checklist for latency bursts (Owner: customer-success)

Medium-term (1–3 months):
- End-to-end trace sampling (user request → kernel dispatch → model exec → response). This is instrument-heavy and needs perf budget. (Owner: observability + serving-runtime)
- Canary UX: show model variant rollout progress and allow ops to pin pinned-variants per-route via Console. (Owner: product-hosted-api + console)

Open questions (need quick answers):
- How easily can serving-runtime add the two headers without changing request latency? (ping: Ben, serving-runtime)
- Do we have sample per-request cache metadata that we can emit cheaply? If not, what’s the perf cost to add it? (ping: SRE infra)
- What database / telemetry indices would Console need to compute per-route cache savings in near-realtime? (ping: observability)

Risks and guardrails:
- Adding verbose telemetry could increase cost; only sample 1% by default and toggleable by customer.
- Exposing fallback reasons may leak internal variant naming; sanitize strings and provide human-friendly labels.

Immediate asks from CS to Eng/Product (actionable items):
- Small spike: implement X-Redwood-Variant header (accepts: variant id) — target: 2 weeks.
- Console quick banner for fallback spikes (>1%) — target: 3 weeks.
- Copy: short help text and support playbook entries for the new signals — target: 1 week after headers land.

Next steps / owners:
- Maya (CS): compile ticket list and sample customer IDs + anonymized request ids for 6 illustrative incidents. (Due: 2026-05-18)
- Diego (Field Eng): validate feasibility of emitting cache-hit per-request metadata; share perf estimate. (Due: 2026-05-20)
- Priya (Product): scope Console UI banner + per-route metric card. Initial mock by 2026-05-24.
- Ben (Serving runtime): prototype header emission on a dev canary; measurement report by 2026-05-21.

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- When we present to ENG triage, bring three customer snippets (one per bucket) + one synthetic timeline showing fallback trigger → routing change.
- Consider a small customer-facing beta: opt-in to verbose telemetry for 1 customer to verify utility without heavy sampling.

Appendix: quick index (tickets / calls referenced)
- Support-8437: RetailGen cache billing question
- Call-2026-05-05: FinSolve onboarding call (recorded)
- Survey: runtime-friction-2026-may (42 responses)

End of working synthesis.

(If useful: I can convert this into a condensed 1-page for Eng TG and a short support script for CS handoff.)
